messages:
Ava (prod-design): Quick design review — updated copy for the 'Stop dedicated pool' confirmation modal. Trying to make consequences clearer (stop vs delete) and call out billing impact. Screenshot: https://redwood.example/screenshot/stop-pool-v3.png

Sam (ux-writer): Nice. Can you paste the current proposed copy here?

Ava (prod-design): Sure — full modal copy below:

```
Header: Stop dedicated pool?
Body: Stopping this pool will immediately halt model serving on the associated GPUs. Your model versions and config will be preserved. You will no longer be billed for active GPU time after the current billing minute completes. Any in-flight requests will be cancelled.
Primary button: Stop pool
Secondary button: Cancel
```

Marco (frontend): Short thoughts — the header reads a bit long and `Stop pool` as the primary verb feels slightly ambiguous (stop vs pause). Are we exposing a pause concept anywhere?

Priya (product): We don't have a formal `pause` feature right now. Operationally stopping releases the GPUs but keeps the pool config so customers can start it again. Important we don't imply a destructive delete.

Sam (ux-writer): Suggest tightening language and reducing passive voice. Also tone — should be firm but not scary. Proposal:

```
Header: Stop pool
Body: This will stop serving and free the GPUs. Your pool settings and model versions will be kept. Billing for GPU time stops after the current minute. Ongoing requests will be cancelled.
Primary button: Stop pool
Secondary button: Go back
```

Olivia (accessibility): A few a11y nits:
- Avoid truncated sentences for screen readers; make sure the body ends with a period.
- Prefer `Stop pool` over `Stop` so button context is clear when read out of context.
- Add aria-describedby linking to the billing sentence so assistive tech can highlight costs.

Marco (frontend): Also: when requests are cancelled, do we return a 503-style error to callers? If so, maybe `in-flight requests will be cancelled` is fine, just flag the API surface so docs can sync.

Priya (product): Yes we return a cancellation error. We should add a one-line microcopy below the modal (smaller, muted) linking to docs: `See what stopping a pool means →` (link).

Sam (ux-writer): Updated compact copy with doc link and shorter header:

```
Header: Stop pool
Body: Stopping this pool will free the GPUs and stop billing after the current minute. Pool settings and model versions will be retained. In-flight requests will be cancelled.
Muted link: See what stopping a pool means →
Primary button: Stop pool
Secondary button: Keep running
```

Ava (prod-design): I like that. A couple of layout asks: make the billing sentence bold or visually prominent? It's important for users to know. Also add a tiny caution icon left of the header. Thoughts?

Olivia (accessibility): Do not rely on visual weight alone for critical info. If you bold the billing line, also include an accessible label or aria-live when the modal opens that announces billing will stop.

Marco (frontend): Bold is fine. We'll also include short aria-live="polite" announcement on modal open with the billing sentence. We can add the link anchor `#stop-pool-docs` to keep it ribbon-friendly.

DesignBot: Automated checks: header length ok, primary button label matches pattern `Verb + target`, color contrast for muted link passes, suggested aria attributes detected in code branch `feature/stop-pool-copy`.

Priya (product): Final call — adopt Sam's compact copy, add muted doc link, bold the billing sentence, include aria-live announcement, and change secondary button to `Keep running`. If no objections I'll merge into the modal PR.

Sam (ux-writer): +1 from me :thumbsup:

Marco (frontend): +1, will implement in the PR and ping when pushed.

Ava (prod-design): Thanks everyone — merging the copy version into the branch now and will update the screenshot in the design system. :sparkles:

Olivia (accessibility): Thanks — please tag me on the PR so I can verify the aria implementation.

Priya (product): Marking as ship-ready once Marco's PR lands.

DesignBot: Linked PR: https://git.redwood/infra/stop-pool-modal/pull/142 — CI checks queued.
